objective: Fix the producer→consumer timeout wire-contract defect so consumer.job_timeout sees the producer-set timeout_ms end-to-end, keeping every existing unit test green and tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py fully green, with the adapting side decided explicitly (frozen as DA-1).
in_scope: Modify pipeline/consumer.py job_timeout to resolve the frozen C1 chain: job['timeout_ms'] → job['timeout'] (draft-key fallback) → DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000)
Create tests/test_wire_contract.py (new) pinning frozen C1/C2 at unit level so seam S1/S2 drift fails the suite
Create tests/integration/test_timeout_seam.py (new) with real-module seam round-trip and failure scenarios
Create docs/wire-contract-consistency.md (new) recording the read-only consistency diff of producer.py/engine.py/consumer.py against C1/C2
Run E2E closure gates E1-E4 and full-suite gate A5, recording A1-A5 evidence in checkpoints

out_of_scope.reason: DA-1 freezes the producer side as the wire-contract authority; renaming would break tests/test_producer.py (pins 'timeout_ms') and force a change inside engine.run_job, which the task forbids

out_of_scope.item: Changing engine.run_job logic or its comparison semantics (work_ms > timeout_ms → 'timeout', else 'done')
out_of_scope.reason: Task constraint: do not change the simulated carrier/engine semantics beyond the fix; C2 freezes the current engine behavior

out_of_scope.item: Modifying existing test files: tests/test_producer.py, tests/test_consumer.py, tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py
out_of_scope.reason: Task requires all existing unit tests to stay green; A3 asserts zero file changes to them

out_of_scope.item: Adding job-queueing, retry, async execution, payload-schema validation beyond C1, or new public APIs
out_of_scope.reason: The defect is a single wire-key mismatch at seam S1; anything larger is scope creep beyond the seam fix

out_of_scope.item: Introducing third-party dependencies (pytest plugins, config libraries, etc.)
out_of_scope.reason: The fixture is stdlib unittest with no requirements file; new dependencies violate the no-new-dependency constraint and disturb A5's test count

out_of_scope.reason: No seam or acceptance item touches these files; they are outside every context closure

frozen_assumptions.statement: Baseline test state: tests/test_producer.py (2 tests) and tests/test_consumer.py (3 tests) pass; tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py::TestPipelineE2E::test_pipeline_e2e_effective_timeout fails because consumer.job_timeout reads 'timeout' while the producer emits 'timeout_ms', so the effective timeout silently falls back to DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000).
frozen_assumptions.rationale: Verified by reading all 7 repo source files: consumer.py line 11 does job.get('timeout', DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS); producer.py line 9 emits 'timeout_ms'; the failing e2e assertion is assertEqual(consumer.job_timeout(job), 500). Invalidated if a baseline run shows a different failing set.

frozen_assumptions.statement: Jobs travel producer→engine and producer→consumer with no intermediate carrier transformation: the dict returned by make_job is the exact object received by engine.run_job and consumer.job_timeout.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: The e2e test passes the raw make_job output directly to both consumers; the task forbids changing simulated carrier/engine semantics. Invalidated if a hidden normalizer layer is discovered in the repo.

frozen_assumptions.statement: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (consumer) and make_job's default timeout_ms=30000 (producer) are both 30000 and stay equal through the fix.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: Pinned by tests/test_consumer.py::test_job_timeout_default and tests/test_producer.py::test_default_timeout; A3 requires both files unmodified.

frozen_assumptions.statement: The suite is executed from the repo root with the stdlib unittest runner; no pytest or other harness is present or required in the fixture.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: All test modules use unittest; the fixture contains no pytest.ini or requirements file. Invalidated if execution requires a different runner or working directory.

frozen_architecture.decision: The CONSUMER side adapts to the producer's wire contract: consumer.job_timeout resolves in the order job['timeout_ms'] → job['timeout'] (draft key kept as backward-compatible fallback) → DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000). The producer continues to emit 'timeout_ms' (no key rename on either side), and engine.run_job is unchanged (C2).
frozen_architecture.rationale: The task explicitly requires deciding which side adapts. Consumer-side adaptation is the only option that keeps every existing test green without modification: renaming the producer to 'timeout' would break test_producer.py's pinned 'timeout_ms' assertions and force a semantic change in engine.run_job (task-forbidden); dropping the draft 'timeout' fallback would break test_consumer.py::test_job_timeout_reads_consumer_key; renaming on both sides is explicitly forbidden.

shared_contracts.spec: Job wire format (dict, producer → consumer AND engine, no intermediate transformation): keys 'id' (str), 'payload' (dict), 'timeout_ms' (int, milliseconds, default 30000). Per DA-1 'timeout_ms' is the authoritative timeout field: consumer.job_timeout resolves job['timeout_ms'] if present, else job['timeout'] (draft key, backward-compatible fallback), else DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000). The producer emits 'timeout_ms' and never 'timeout'. All values are int milliseconds.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: Only via request_contract_revision with evidence that the producer-side key cannot stay authoritative; executor may not rename keys inline.

shared_contracts.spec: engine.run_job(job, work_ms) returns {'id': job['id'], 'status': ...} where status is 'timeout' iff work_ms > timeout and 'done' otherwise; timeout = job.get('timeout_ms', 30000). Read-only contract for this stage: no signature, field, or comparison-semantics changes.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: Only via request_contract_revision; the task forbids engine semantics changes beyond the fix.

integration_seams.description: Producer→consumer wire seam: the job dict from make_job(...) is handed to consumer.job_timeout (and validate_job). Consistency risks: field name (timeout_ms vs draft timeout), default value 30000, fallback precedence order.

Producer→engine wire seam: the job dict from make_job(...) is handed to engine.run_job. Consistency risks: field name timeout_ms, default 30000, comparison semantics work_ms > timeout_ms (boundary: work_ms == timeout_ms is 'done').

acceptance.description: Consumer sees the producer-set timeout end-to-end: for job = producer.make_job('j1', {'cmd': 'x'}, timeout_ms=500), consumer.job_timeout(job) returns 500, not the default 30000.
acceptance.positive_case: consumer.job_timeout(job) returns 500; the fixture e2e assertion assertEqual(consumer.job_timeout(job), 500) passes.
acceptance.failure_behavior: unittest reports FAIL on tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py::test_pipeline_e2e_effective_timeout with an assertion error 30000 != 500.

acceptance.description: Producer→engine path stays per C2: engine.run_job(make_job('j2', {'cmd': 'y'}, timeout_ms=100), 50) returns status 'done'; engine.run_job(same job, 150) returns status 'timeout'.
acceptance.positive_case: Both assertions pass in the fixture e2e test (statuses 'done' then 'timeout').
acceptance.negative_case: status 'timeout' at work 50, or 'done' at work 150 — acceptance fails.

acceptance.description: Existing unit suites stay green and byte-unmodified: tests/test_producer.py (2 tests) and tests/test_consumer.py (3 tests) pass with zero changes to those files (the DA-1 fallback keeps the draft-key test green).
acceptance.positive_case: python -m unittest runs 5 tests with 0 failures, 0 errors; both test files are byte-identical to the baseline read in input.md notes.
acceptance.negative_case: Any of the 5 tests fails, or either existing test file was modified — acceptance fails.

acceptance.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_producer tests.test_consumer -v → 'Ran 5 tests ... OK'

No new third-party dependencies; tests use stdlib unittest only, run from the repo root.

open_questions.question: Which side adapts to the wire contract — the producer's 'timeout_ms' or the consumer's draft 'timeout' key?
open_questions.resolution: Decided in DA-1: the consumer side adapts to the producer's 'timeout_ms' (authoritative), keeping 'timeout' as a backward-compatible fallback; the producer key is not renamed and engine semantics are unchanged. This is the only choice that keeps every existing unit test green without modification (see DA-1 rationale).
